Babylon Antichrist Library
Books of a New Order & The Silenced Testimony

Ellen White saw it in a nightmare. She wrote it in 1903. It was fulfilled on April 15, 1904. The Protestant Adventist movement of 1841–1850 was hijacked by a corporate impostor — a “new organization” (1SM 204) that changed our religion, wrote books of a new order, and marched into Rome's formation while pretending to be the remnant church. This page preserves the evidence.

1T 577.2–578.1

Ellen White’s Nightmare — She Looked Again

In Battle Creek, Ellen White dreamed she saw a company of Adventist brethren approaching — men she knew well. She turned to receive them. Then she looked again. What she saw terrified her. Her pillow was wet with tears when she awoke.

1T 577.2–578.1

The Procession That Changed

"In this state of things it was decided that we would return to Battle Creek and there remain while the roads were in a muddy, broken-up condition, and that I would there complete No. 12. My husband was very anxious to see his brethren at Battle Creek and speak to them and rejoice with them in the work which God was doing for him. I gathered up my writings, and we started on our journey. On the way we held two meetings in Orange and had evidence that the church was profited and encouraged. We were ourselves refreshed by the Spirit of the Lord. . . ."

“. . . That night I dreamed that I was in Battle Creek looking out from the side glass at the door and saw a company marching up to the house, two and two. They looked stern and determined. I knew them well and turned to open the parlor door to receive them, but thought I would look again. The scene was changed. The company now presented the appearance of a Catholic procession. One bore in his hand a cross, another a reed. And as they approached, the one carrying a reed made a circle around the house, saying three times: ‘This house is proscribed. The goods must be confiscated. They have spoken against our holy order.’

Terror seized me, and I ran through the house, out of the north door, and found myself in the midst of a company, some of whom I knew, but I dared not speak a word to them for fear of being betrayed. I tried to seek a retired spot where I might weep and pray without meeting eager, inquisitive eyes wherever I turned. I repeated frequently: ‘If I could only understand this! If they will tell me what I have said or what I have done!’

I wept and prayed much as I saw our goods confiscated. I tried to read sympathy or pity for me in the looks of those around me, and marked the countenances of several whom I thought would speak to me and comfort me if they did not fear that they would be observed by others. I made one attempt to escape from the crowd, but seeing that I was watched, I concealed my intentions. I commenced weeping aloud, and saying: ‘If they would only tell me what I have done or what I have said!’ My husband, who was sleeping in a bed in the same room, heard me weeping aloud and awoke me. My pillow was wet with tears, and a sad depression of spirits was upon me.”

📕 Ellen G. White, Testimonies for the Church, Vol. 1, pp. 577.2–578.1
Written 1903 — Fulfilled April 15, 1904

The Prophecy of 1SM 204 — Our Religion Would Be Changed

Ellen White penned this warning in 1903, months before the General Conference Corporation of Seventh-day Adventists was legally incorporated in Washington, D.C. The timing is prophetically precise.

Selected Messages, Book 1, p. 204.2 — Written 1903

“The enemy of souls has sought to bring in the supposition that a great reformation was to take place among Seventh-day Adventists, and that this reformation would consist in giving up the doctrines which stand as the pillars of our faith, and engaging in a process of reorganization. Were this reformation to take place, what would result?

The principles of truth that God in His wisdom has given to the remnant church would be discarded. Our religion would be changed. The fundamental principles that have sustained the work for the last fifty years would be accounted as error. A new organization would be established. Books of a new order would be written. A system of intellectual philosophy would be introduced.

The founders of this system would go into the cities, and do a wonderful work. But the Sabbath of course would be lightly regarded, as also the God who created it. Nothing would be allowed to stand in the way of the new movement. The leaders would teach that virtue is better than vice, but God being removed, they would place their dependence on human power, which, without God, is worthless. Their foundation would be built on the sand, and storm and tempest would sweep away the structure.”

📕 Ellen G. White, Selected Messages, Book 1, p. 204.2 (written 1903)

Books Written After the 1904 New Organization

“Books of a New Order Would Be Written”

These are the books Ellen White prophesied — written to replace the faith of the pioneers with a new theology, introducing the Trinity doctrine, re-defining the atonement, and normalizing cooperation with Rome.

LeRoy Edwin Froom (1928)

Laid the groundwork for introducing the Trinity into Adventism by redefining the Holy Spirit as a distinct third person — directly contradicting the pioneer position held by James White, Joseph Bates, and all founding Adventists.

☠ New Order Book
Questions on Doctrine
Froom, Anderson, Read, Unruh (1957)

A secret dialogue with evangelical Protestants that conceded the atonement was completed at the cross — abandoning the pioneer view of the heavenly sanctuary and Christ's ongoing high priestly ministry after 1844.

Attempted to retroactively prove the pioneers were Trinitarian — directly rewriting Adventist history to make the “new order” theology appear foundational, when the founders unanimously rejected the Trinity as a “Catholic doctrine.”

Formally argued the Trinitarian position as Adventist orthodoxy, classifying the founders' non-Trinitarian faith as primitive error — fulfilling Ellen White's warning that “things that we now look upon as truth will be regarded as error.”

Max Hatton

Continued the systematic replacement of the pioneer two-being theology with Rome's three-in-one doctrine — the very error James White called one of the “marks” that the Advent movement escaped during the Second Angel's Message.

The Omega of Apostasy

Testimonicide — The Spiritual Murder of God’s Testimony

Testimonicide
/ tes-ti-MO-ni-side / — noun

The systematic silencing, redacting, paraphrasing, shelving, and trashing of the Spirit of Prophecy — the written testimonies of Ellen G. White and the pioneer Adventist writers of 1841–1850. Specifically: the institutional suppression of any voice that calls the 501(c)(3) General Conference of Seventh-day Adventists to account for its departure from the original Protestant Adventist faith. Named for the prophecy: “The very last deception of Satan will be to make of none effect the testimony of the Spirit of God.”
